sermon.title: The Lord is My Shepherd
sermon.speaker: Pastor David G. Kincer
sermon.summary: Pastor David G. Kincer closes his series on the first and great commandment with Psalm 23, King David’s personal account of following the Shepherd despite enemies, betrayals and flaws. Each line shows a benefit: no lack, rest, the Spirit’s living water, restoration, righteous paths, no fear, a table before enemies, an overflowing cup, goodness and mercy. The key is to make him your Shepherd and apply what you learn.
sermon.transcript_source: This transcript comes from YouTube’s automatic English captions, which supply the timing and the words. Punctuation, capitalization and paragraphing were added from the speaker’s pauses and then corrected by hand, and obvious caption errors (names, Bible references) were fixed; his wording was not rewritten. “[unclear]” marks a word or name that was not clear. Editor notes: Points to check: David “no more than 14” killing the lion and bear by hand; God “would not forgive the shedding of innocent blood” called an unpardonable sin forgiven; Elijah’s barrels and the widow’s vessels (Elisha in 2 Kings 4); tongues “three out of four times.” Sensitive content kept as spoken: atheists and secular humanists; public schools; liberals and socialists; James Dobson and Peyton Manning named; moral Catholics “though they have idols.”

chunks.section_question: Why end the series with Psalm 23?
chunks.short_answer: This last session on the first and great commandment goes to Psalm 23, where King David gives a personal account of following the Shepherd and its benefits. David was handsome, a skilled musician, warrior, businessman and speaker—so serving God is not just a crutch for weak people.

faqs.question: Is faith only for weak people?
faqs.answer: No—David was handsome, skilled and courageous.

faqs.question: Is any sin unforgivable?
faqs.answer: He says no sin cannot be forgiven, as with David.

faqs.question: Does God promise riches?
faqs.answer: No—he promises food, clothing, shelter and every good thing.

faqs.question: Is the baptism of the Holy Ghost for today?
Is tongues the only initial evidence?
faqs.answer: He says the Bible never says that.

faqs.question: Does God discipline his sheep?
faqs.answer: Yes, but he doesn’t cast them away.

faqs.question: Can you lose the anointing?
faqs.answer: He says they didn’t lose it when they washed.

faqs.question: Should church workers expect pay?
faqs.answer: He says your pay is the word and Spirit of God.
